It had a same-planet guard (his 10-15 pick) and that guard CRASHED the game at startquest (his play, 2026-10-19); his ruling: no planet guards, 'it's fine if the mission is on the same planet'. second._fill: OT-03's late same-system fill (his 'MB42a takes the late-fill shape'), and his small-delivery rule: not across the map.

place._theme: A wreck here; the delivery site must never be a wreck itself (two places that could draw one POI warn). ELIZA 2026-10-15, measured: a request can put down 3 wreck sites of 214, so every crash site is one of three; the board places it, so it always starts.

message.title: Wreck Cargo Crate
message.text: The crate's seals are scorched, but they held.

beats.journal: I got the freighter's crate out from under the spacers at the <Place>. I need to take it to the station it was meant for.

beats.objective: Deliver the crate to the station's keeper

person.name: Odette Vane
hellos: Is that crate scorched? Please tell me it's not scorched inside.

_bio.from: keeps a small station running alone (her lines)
_bio.why_there: the station, on its backup for a month while the coupling was in transit (her lines)
_bio.wants: the lights back on, and the freighter's crew remembered (her lines)

greeting: You've brought my coupling. We've been running on the backup for a month, and the backup was never meant to run a week.

exchanges.prompt: Here's your crate. The seals held.
reply: The seals held. So did we, just about. I'll have the lights back on before you've left orbit.

exchanges.prompt: The freighter went down with it.
reply: I heard. I sent word to the crew's families this morning. It felt wrong to sit here and only wait for a crate.

beats.journal: A freighter went down at the <Place> and spacers were picking over the wreck. I got the consignment out from under them and put it in the hands of the station keeper it was meant for.
